title: Asking Smarter Questions: Targeted Active Preference Learning for Underspecified Rewards
abstract: arXiv:2610.22285v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reward learning typically assumes the human's input covers everything that matters for the task. In practice, humans can only attend to so much at once, so their teaching naturally captures some features---or aspects of the task---better than others. Prior work has shown how the robot can identify which features were poorly supervised directly from its teaching data. But the current solution is to ask the human to try again, putting the burden on someone who already struggled to convey those features. We propose shifting this burden to the robot. Our key insight is that the same information that tells the robot what it doesn't know can help it ask better questions. Preference queries offer a low-effort channel for resolving this uncertainty, but only if the robot knows where to direct them and the human knows what to attend to when answering. We act on this insight in two ways: we build an informed prior that targets preference queries

translated_title: 提问更聪明的问题：面向欠规范奖励的定向主动偏好学习
translated_abstract: 奖励学习通常假设人类的输入涵盖了任务中所有重要的内容。但在实践中，人类一次只能关注有限的方面，因此他们的教学自然会对任务的某些特征——即某些方面——的捕捉效果优于其他方面。先前的工作已经展示了机器人如何直接从教学数据中识别出哪些特征未得到充分监督。然而，目前的解决方案是让人类重新进行教学，这将负担压在了那些本来就在传达这些特征时遇到困难的人身上。我们提出将这一负担转移给机器人。我们的关键洞察是：那些告诉机器人自己不知道什么的信息，同样可以帮助它提出更好的问题。偏好查询为解决这种不确定性提供了一种低成本的渠道，但前提是机器人知道该将查询定向到何处，并且人类在回答时知道该关注什么。我们通过两种方式践行这一洞察：首先，我们构建了一个有信息量的先验，将偏好查询定向到……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将澄清欠规范奖励的负担从人类转移给机器人，利用教学数据中揭示不确定性的信息构建有针对性的先验，通过定向偏好查询让人类以低成本方式弥补监督不足的任务特征。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes shifting the burden of clarifying underspecified rewards from humans to robots, which leverage the same information revealing their uncertainty to build an informed prior that targets preference queries, enabling humans to efficiently resolve poorly supervised task features.
